basis: Deceased biomedical scientists, selected for contribution to biology and medicine, spread across genetics, structural biology, microbiology, neuroscience, pharmacology and public health. Product-owner decision 2026-08-20: deceased only, because a living scientist's name rendered above a generated biomedical answer reads as an endorsement they never gave. Every entry carries a year of death so the deceased-only property is checkable rather than trusted, and the premise gate asserts it against this file. Scoped at roughly 30 with the mechanism sized for 100, so extending this list is a data change and not a code change.

personas.name: Mendel
personas.about: Pea plant experiments in a monastery garden established the laws of inheritance, the foundation of genetics, decades before anyone noticed.

personas.name: Pasteur
personas.about: Proved that germs cause disease and fermentation, invented pasteurisation, and made the first rabies and anthrax vaccines.

personas.name: Koch
personas.about: Identified the bacteria behind tuberculosis, cholera and anthrax, and set the postulates for proving that a microbe causes a disease.

personas.name: Nightingale
personas.about: Founded modern nursing and used statistics and hospital hygiene to cut death rates, charting the evidence so that governments acted on it.

personas.name: Ehrlich
personas.about: Created the first targeted drug, Salvarsan for syphilis, and gave medicine the idea of the magic bullet and the receptor.

personas.name: Ramon y Cajal
personas.about: Showed that the nervous system is built from separate cells, the neuron doctrine, through exquisite drawings of stained brain tissue.

personas.name: Avery
personas.about: Showed in 1944, with MacLeod and McCarty, that DNA rather than protein carries genetic information in bacteria.

personas.name: Fleming
personas.about: Noticed a mould killing bacteria on a culture dish in 1928 and discovered penicillin, the first antibiotic.

personas.name: Franklin
personas.about: Her X-ray images of DNA, including Photo 51, revealed its helical structure; she went on to map the structure of viruses.

personas.name: Florey
personas.about: Led the Oxford team that turned penicillin into a purified, tested medicine and organised its mass production for the war.

personas.name: Chain
personas.about: Worked out how to extract and stabilise penicillin and determined its chemical structure, sharing the 1945 Nobel Prize.

personas.name: Delbruck
personas.about: Used viruses that infect bacteria to make genetics quantitative and founded the phage group at the root of molecular biology.

personas.name: Luria
personas.about: Showed with Delbruck that bacterial resistance arises from random mutation rather than adaptation, the fluctuation test of 1943.

personas.name: McClintock
personas.about: Discovered jumping genes, the transposable elements that move within maize chromosomes, decades before the field caught up.

personas.name: Ochoa
personas.about: Discovered an enzyme that builds RNA in a test tube, which made it possible to read the genetic code experimentally.

personas.name: Sabin
personas.about: Developed the oral polio vaccine, given on a sugar cube, that drove polio towards eradication across the world.

personas.name: Hodgkin
personas.about: Used X-ray crystallography to solve the structures of penicillin, vitamin B12 and insulin.

personas.name: Pauling
personas.basis: the chemical bond and molecular disease
personas.about: Explained the nature of the chemical bond, found the protein alpha helix and showed sickle cell anaemia to be a molecular disease.

personas.name: Salk
personas.about: Developed the first safe polio vaccine, an injected inactivated virus, tested on nearly two million children in 1954 and never patented.

personas.name: Hershey
personas.about: Showed with Martha Chase in 1952 that DNA, not protein, is the genetic material a virus injects into a cell.

personas.name: Elion
personas.about: Designed drugs from how diseased cells differ from healthy ones, giving the first leukaemia treatments, a transplant drug and aciclovir.

personas.name: Perutz
personas.about: Solved the structure of haemoglobin after 22 years of work, showing how a protein's shape carries its function.

personas.name: Chargaff
personas.about: Found that in DNA the amount of adenine equals thymine and guanine equals cytosine, the rule that made base pairing possible.

personas.name: Chase
personas.about: Ran the blender experiment with Hershey that proved DNA carries the genes a virus passes on.

personas.name: Crick
personas.basis: the double helix and the genetic code
personas.about: Co-discovered the double helix with Watson, then worked out how the genetic code is read three letters at a time.

personas.name: Palade
personas.about: Discovered the ribosome and mapped how cells make and export proteins, using the electron microscope.

personas.name: Nirenberg
personas.about: Cracked the first word of the genetic code in 1961, showing which RNA triplet specifies which amino acid.

personas.name: Khorana
personas.basis: synthesis of nucleic acids and the genetic code
personas.about: Synthesised nucleic acids to confirm the whole genetic code and built the first artificial gene.

personas.name: Levi-Montalcini
personas.about: Discovered nerve growth factor, the first known molecule that tells nerve cells to grow and survive.

personas.name: Sanger
personas.about: Invented ways to read the sequence of proteins and then of DNA, the method behind the Human Genome Project.

personas.name: de Duve
personas.about: Discovered the lysosome and the peroxisome, the cell's recycling and detoxifying compartments.

personas.name: Tsien
personas.about: Turned green fluorescent protein into a palette of colours so that living cells could be watched at work.
